question: What does a black, tarry stool sample usually tell you about your patient?

options.A: Bleeding in the upper gastrointestinal tract
options.B: Bleeding in the lower rectum or anus
options.C: Severe dehydration and low fluid intake
options.D: A high intake of green leafy vegetables

question: Why do premature babies often have trouble getting their ductus arteriosus to close?

options.C: Their liver produces excessive amounts of bile that block circulation
options.D: Their left atrium has too much pressure compared to the right atrium

question: What simple physical technique can a patient use to stop a faint when they first feel warning symptoms?

options.B: Massaging both sides of the neck firmly
options.C: Holding the breath for as long as possible
options.D: Crossing the legs and tensing the muscles

question: Why do we call patient assessment in the intensive care unit a continuous loop?

options.A: Because vital signs never change in stable patients
options.B: Because doctors only visit patients once a day
options.C: Because hospital computers demand hourly data entry
options.D: Because interventions require constant re-evaluation

question: How can you easily tell chronic pain apart from acute pain?

options.A: Chronic pain always responds better to opioids
options.B: Chronic pain lasts longer than three to six months
options.C: Chronic pain originates exclusively from skin tissue
options.D: Chronic pain disappears rapidly after tissue healing

question: What is the best initial nursing action if a patient has a painful ingrown toenail that looks a bit red?

question: How can an unusually long fallopian tube affect the movement of an egg?

question: What is the main focus of 'validity' when creating a research tool?

options.C: How cheap the research instrument is to buy in bulk

question: A newborn is getting PPV, but their heart rate is still 70 and their chest isn't moving. What should you check first?

options.A: Increase the oxygen concentration to 100 percent
options.B: Insert an umbilical venous catheter for epinephrine
options.C: Check and adjust the mask seal and head position
options.D: Immediately begin emergency chest compressions

question: A patient arrives with a small piece of metal stuck deep inside their eyeball. What must you NEVER do?

options.A: Call the eye doctor right away

options.C: Attempt to pull or remove the embedded metal piece

question: What can happen if a nurse rudely dismisses a patient for using traditional local remedies?

options.A: The hospital will automatically discharge the patient for misconduct
options.B: Local herbalists will protest outside the hospital gates
options.C: The patient will instantly abandon all traditional beliefs forever
options.D: The patient may hide information or delay seeking crucial medical help

question: What is the main difference between curative treatment and palliative care?

options.A: Curative treatment aims to eradicate disease, while palliative care focuses on comfort and quality of life.

options.C: Curative treatment ignores physical pain, while palliative care focuses only on surgery.
options.D: Curative treatment is provided at home, while palliative care requires an intensive care unit.

explanation: Think of it this way: curative treatment fights the disease itself to get rid of it, while palliative care fights the discomfort and pain so the patient can feel better day-to-day. You've got this! [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h3)

question: Why is it so important to screen and care for depression during neuro-rehab?

options.A: Family members do not experience any stress as long as the client feels physically comfortable.

options.C: Psychological distress is contagious and often spreads quickly among other clients in the ward.
options.D: Emotional symptoms are always temporary and disappear completely without any professional intervention.

question: Why is a patient scheduled for an abdominal ultrasound usually told to fast (no food or water) for a few hours beforehand?

options.A: To keep their blood pressure steady before the scan

options.C: To make sure they have an empty bladder for a pelvic check
options.D: To stop them from throwing up during the procedure

question: Which report from a postpartum mother at home means she needs to see a doctor urgently?

question: Why is IEC such an important strategy in primary health care?

options.A: It replaces the need for administering routine childhood immunizations.

options.C: It allows nurses to diagnose complex tropical diseases without a doctor.

question: How do soaps and surfactants mainly destroy germs on the skin?

question: What is the main purpose of the clay and plastic lining inside a sanitary landfill?

options.A: To keep the landfill smelling fresh for nearby communities

question: At what fill level should a clinical sharps container be securely closed and replaced?

question: Which common group of over-the-counter painkillers must patients with kidney disease strictly avoid?

question: What happens immediately to your body when stress hormones like adrenaline rush into your bloodstream?

question: Why do we need good 'organising' skills after making a nursing care plan?

question: Why are the normal bacteria living inside your large intestine so important?

question: Why is psychological support also offered to the family members of a recovering patient?

question: Why do birth attendants need to be extra careful if an episiotomy is done near vulval varicosities?

options.A: Dilated blood vessels tend to bleed much more heavily when cut
options.B: Cutting the skin will cause permanent nerve paralysis in the leg
options.C: Local anaesthetic injections will not work near swollen tissues
options.D: The wound will never heal properly due to poor local hygiene

explanation: Engorged veins are full of blood under pressure. Cutting near them requires extra caution because they can bleed quite heavily. You're building great clinical intuition! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T9#GNS216_U5_T9_h6)

question: What is an important nursing check after a patient has an upper GI scope (endoscopy)?

options.A: Giving strong oral laxatives to clear out remaining dye
options.B: Putting warm compresses on the tummy every 15 minutes
options.C: Checking that the patient's gag reflex is back before giving food or water
options.D: Pushing the patient to eat a heavy meal right away to get their strength back

explanation: The throat spray numbs the back of the throat during the scope. If you feed them before the gag reflex returns, they could easily choke or aspirate. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h7)

question: When we talk about 'sex' in human health, what are we mainly referring to?

options.A: Physical and physiological traits
options.B: Cultural roles assigned at birth
options.C: Socially constructed behaviors
options.D: Personal expressions of identity

explanation: You've got this! 'Sex' refers to our biological makeup—like chromosomes, hormones, and anatomy—which is different from the social roles we play. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T3#GNS312_U4_T3_h1)

question: What do we call wound drainage that is clear and watery?

options.A: Sanguineous
options.B: Fibrinous
options.C: Purulent
options.D: Serous

explanation: Serous fluid comes from plasma—think of the clear liquid you see in a minor blister. Easy terminology to lock down! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h4)

question: What yummy nickname is often given to old, dark blood-filled cysts found on the ovaries in endometriosis?

options.A: Chocolate cysts
options.B: Serous cystadenomas
options.C: Dermoid tumors
options.D: Fibroid nodules

explanation: They are called 'chocolate cysts' because the old, trapped menstrual blood inside turns dark brown and thick, looking a bit like melted chocolate! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T21#GNS216_U5_T21_h3)

question: When you gently tap and feel a patient's arm to find a good vein, what should a healthy peripheral vein feel like?

options.A: A hard, rigid cord that does not bounce back
options.B: A soft, bouncy vessel that refills after being pressed
options.C: A deep vessel that cannot be felt but looks dark blue
options.D: A pulsing vessel that moves strongly under the finger

explanation: Spot on! Healthy veins feel spongy, elastic, and refill promptly with blood after you press them. You'll get great at spotting these on the ward! [learn more](GNS311_U4_T6#GNS311_U4_T6_h2)

question: Between which two meningeal layers is the subarachnoid space located?

options.A: Bone and dura mater
options.B: Arachnoid mater and pia mater
options.C: Dura mater and arachnoid mater
options.D: Skin and subcutaneous tissue

explanation: The subarachnoid space sits specifically between the middle arachnoid layer and the innermost pia mater layer. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h2)

question: Why do clinicians often use resting metabolic rate (RMR) instead of basal metabolic rate (BMR)?

options.A: It completely excludes the energy used by internal organs
options.B: It is always identical to total daily energy expenditure
options.C: It measures the exact calories burned during running
options.D: It requires fewer strict laboratory conditions to measure

explanation: Great job! RMR is much more practical in hospital and clinic settings because it doesn't force the patient to go through a strict 12-hour fast and absolute rest like BMR does. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T008#GNS227_U4_T008_h2)

question: What is the main reason for using aseptic technique during surgery?

options.A: To reduce the cost of surgical supplies
options.B: To make the surgical room smell clean
options.C: To eliminate all micro-organisms from the surgical field
options.D: To speed up the recovery time after anesthesia

explanation: Great job! Aseptic technique blocks germs and bad bugs from getting into the patient's vulnerable body tissues. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h5)

question: What outdated myth sometimes stops providers from offering IUDs to young people?

options.A: The assumption that IUDs stop the user's heart from beating
options.B: The belief that IUDs are only safe for women who have children
options.C: The fear that IUDs permanently cure all forms of pelvic pain
options.D: The idea that IUDs require refrigeration before clinical insertion

explanation: Current clinical guidelines confirm that IUDs are safe and effective for adolescents, even if they haven't had children yet. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T10#GNS312_U3_T10_h4)

question: Why is the brain hit the hardest when someone experiences asphyxia?

options.A: It has a high metabolic rate and constant oxygen demand
options.B: It produces its own oxygen through cellular division
options.C: It stores large reserves of backup oxygen
options.D: It is protected by cerebrospinal fluid that blocks toxins

explanation: The brain is a busy organ that constantly demands oxygen. When that supply cuts off, brain cells start struggling almost immediately. Great job reviewing this! [learn more](GNS221_U3_T6#GNS221_U3_T6_h1)

question: Why do nurses recommend routine STI screenings for sexually active teens even when they feel completely fine?

options.A: Pathogens disappear on their own within one week.
options.B: Many common infections do not show any noticeable symptoms.
options.C: Symptoms only appear after permanent organ damage occurs.
options.D: Testing builds immunity against future pathogen exposures.

explanation: Exactly! Infections like chlamydia are often 'silent' or asymptomatic in young people, so testing is the only way to catch them early. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T15#GNS312_U3_T15_h3)

question: During non-surgical care for a kidney injury, which nursing sign is most important to report immediately?

options.A: An increase in sleepiness after receiving a scheduled pain medication
options.B: Mild bruising fading to a yellow color around the flank area
options.C: A sudden drop in blood pressure paired with a fast heart rate
options.D: A slight yellow tinge in the normal daily urine output

explanation: A fast heart rate and dropping blood pressure are early warning signs of hidden internal bleeding. Catching this early can save a life! [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h6)

question: When planning exercises for a patient whose cancer has spread to the bones, what must you guard against?

options.A: Respiratory alkalosis
options.B: Pathological fractures
options.C: Acute kidney injury
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: Bones weakened by cancer metastases are very fragile. We must avoid high-impact movements to prevent unexpected bone breaks. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T11#GNS321_U1_T11_h6)

question: What are the three classic signs of Wernicke encephalopathy?

options.A: Chest pain, high fever, and skin rash
options.B: Tremors, stiffness, and slow movement
options.C: Eye problems, poor balance, and confusion
options.D: Severe headache, stiff neck, and sudden paralysis

explanation: Great job! Watch out for trouble with eye movements, unsteady walking, and confusion—they form the classic triad. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T7#GNS222_U4_T7_h4)

question: What do we call the grief family members feel *before* their loved one actually passes away?

options.A: Post-mortem grief
options.B: Anticipatory grief
options.C: Acute distress syndrome
options.D: Complicated grief

explanation: It's called anticipatory grief because the family is already mourning the expected loss while the patient is still alive and fighting. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T8#GNS221_U4_T8_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal use for sedative medications?

options.A: Treating bacterial infections
options.B: Stopping active epileptic seizures
options.C: Managing acute and chronic anxiety
options.D: Inducing sleep during short-term insomnia

explanation: Sedatives only calm the nervous system. They do not kill bacteria—that is a job for antibiotics! [learn more](GNS223_U6_T2#GNS223_U6_T2_h4)

question: Why do many nurses feel more emotional weight when turning off a ventilator compared to deciding not to start one?

options.A: Because stopping an active machine feels like a direct action causing death
options.B: Because hospital policies strictly forbid withdrawing mechanical ventilation
options.C: Because family members are never allowed to witness ventilator removal
options.D: Because withholding treatment requires more paperwork than withdrawing

explanation: Physically reaching out to switch off life support feels heavy emotionally, even though ethically and legally, letting nature take its course is the same in both cases. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T7#GNS321_U4_T7_h4)

question: Which of these is a standard pre-procedure nursing duty before an EPS?

options.A: Verifying that informed consent has been properly obtained
options.B: Keeping the patient running on a treadmill for a stress baseline
options.C: Permanently implanting a pacemaker before the test
options.D: Administering a double dose of blood thinners that morning

explanation: As a nurse, making sure the patient understands the procedure and has signed their consent form is a vital safety step every single time. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T10#GNS222_U3_T10_h3)

question: Which of these means a patient should NOT have an IVP done?

options.A: Severe allergy to iodine or contrast dye
options.B: Mild controlled essential hypertension
options.C: A diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus
options.D: A history of childhood asthma

explanation: Safety first! If a patient has a severe iodine allergy, injecting the contrast dye could trigger a dangerous allergic reaction. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T16#GNS221_U2_T16_h3)

question: Which laboratory test is most commonly used to monitor a patient taking warfarin?

options.A: White blood cell differential
options.B: Total red blood cell count
options.C: Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time
options.D: Prothrombin Time and INR

explanation: Prothrombin Time and its standardized INR ratio are the standard tests used to track the effectiveness of warfarin therapy. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h7)

question: What structure marks the point where nerve fibers exit the eye to form the optic nerve?

options.A: Optic disc
options.B: Pupil
options.C: Retina
options.D: Macula

explanation: The optic disc is the anatomical convergence point where nerve fibers leave the eye and appears as a yellowish-pink structure during the exam. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h2)

question: What is a common emotional challenge faced by patients stuck in long-term isolation?

options.A: Complete loss of long-term memory
options.B: A sudden increase in physical stamina
options.C: Total indifference to hospital surroundings
options.D: Feelings of loneliness and anxiety

explanation: That's right. Being cut off from loved ones and normal human contact can feel really heavy, so our emotional support matters just as much as medical care! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is the most critical nursing action for a patient with a continuous bladder irrigation (CBI) catheter after prostate surgery?

options.A: Removing the indwelling catheter immediately on postoperative day one
options.B: Restricting oral fluid intake to keep the drainage bag from filling
options.C: Clamping the catheter tube every hour to measure bladder capacity
options.D: Monitoring urine output color and clearing any clots to prevent blockage

explanation: You got it! CBI keeps blood clots from plugging up the catheter. As a nurse, watching the drainage color and keeping the lines clear prevents painful bladder spasms and blockages. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T11#GNS311_U1_T11_h7)

question: A new mother is worried about straining on the toilet with her stitches. What is the best advice to give her?

options.A: Restrict fluid intake so you do not need to go as often
options.B: Avoid eating solid food for the first two weeks
options.C: Hold your breath and push firmly to finish quickly
options.D: Eat plenty of high-fiber foods and drink plenty of fluids

explanation: Wonderful advice! Fiber and water keep stools soft, preventing constipation so she won't have to strain and hurt her healing tissues. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T12#GNS121_U5_T12_h7)

question: What combination must be strictly avoided when a patient is taking an opioid cough medicine like codeine?

options.A: Topical skin creams for dry hands
options.B: Plain water or unsweetened fruit juice
options.C: Alcohol or central nervous system sedatives
options.D: Low-sodium salt substitutes in food

explanation: Mixing opioids with alcohol or other sedatives causes dangerous drowsiness and can even stop a patient from breathing. Safety first! [learn more](GNS223_U2_T1#GNS223_U2_T1_h6)

question: Which enzyme do corticosteroids block to stop the body's inflammatory process?

options.A: Phospholipase A2
options.B: Cyclooxygenase-2
options.C: Acetylcholinesterase
options.D: Beta-lactamase

explanation: Spot on! Steroids block phospholipase A2 right at the beginning of the inflammation pathway, which stops inflammatory chemicals from ever forming. You've got this! [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h1)

question: Which adaptive tool helps a patient with shaky hands eat on their own?

options.A: A long-handled reacher
options.B: Weighted utensils
options.C: A mechanical lift
options.D: A rigid gait belt

explanation: You got it! Heavy spoons and forks help steady shaky hands so food actually makes it to the mouth. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T5#GNS123_U6_T5_h5)

question: Which mental health challenges most commonly first appear during the teenage years?

options.A: Senile dementia and delirium
options.B: Post-partum psychosis
options.C: Depression and anxiety
options.D: Severe cognitive regression

explanation: Well done! Because of all the massive body changes and social stress, depression and anxiety often peak or first show up during these years. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T3#GNS312_U3_T3_h6)

question: Why don't a mother's breathing parameters snap back to normal the exact day she gives birth?

options.A: Hormones like progesterone disappear from the bloodstream within seconds
options.B: The uterus remains completely enlarged forever after pregnancy
options.C: Chest wall and lung tissues need time to recover their normal shape and compliance
options.D: Postpartum blood loss always causes chronic lung damage

explanation: The pressure lifts right away, but the stretched rib cage and muscles need a few weeks to bounce back. Keep up the great studying! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T3#GNS121_U7_T3_h6)

question: What is one of the most important daily fluid instructions to give a patient managing gout?

options.A: Drink plenty of water daily
options.B: Only drink liquids during mealtimes
options.C: Avoid water and drink soda instead
options.D: Restrict all fluids to prevent swelling

explanation: Correct! Drinking lots of water helps the kidneys flush out extra uric acid before it has a chance to form stubborn crystals. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h7)

question: Which tool is best for measuring the standing height of an adult patient?

options.A: Knee height calipers
options.B: An infant length board
options.C: A stadiometer
options.D: A flexible cloth sewing tape

explanation: A stadiometer is the standard tool with a vertical backboard and sliding headpiece built specifically to measure standing height accurately. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T3#GNS112_U6_T3_h3)

question: What is a major requirement for medical equipment used inside an aircraft?

options.A: It must be lightweight and battery-operated
options.B: It must be made entirely of glass and porcelain
options.C: It must be larger than standard hospital monitors
options.D: It must plug directly into standard wall sockets

explanation: Brilliant! Space and power are limited in aircraft, so all gear has to be portable, light, and run smoothly on reliable batteries. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T14#GNS321_U2_T14_h5)

question: Why are elderly individuals at higher risk for severe burn injuries from hot water?

options.A: Their skin is thinner and loses sensitivity
options.B: They prefer much hotter bath temperatures
options.C: Their homes lack modern plumbing systems
options.D: They spend more time cooking than younger adults

explanation: Thinning skin and reduced nerve sensitivity mean older adults may not feel extreme heat quickly enough to pull away. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h4)

question: What is the main goal of public health surveillance?

options.A: To continuously track health data and spot where diseases are hiding
options.B: To make cheap medicines for rural clinics
options.C: To diagnose patients with long-term mental illness
options.D: To punish hospitals that miss their cleaning schedules

explanation: Surveillance is like keeping a watchful eye on community health trends so we can catch outbreaks before they blow up. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T5#GNS313_U1_T5_h7)

question: A nurse picks up a sterile surgical tray from the supply room and notices the outer paper wrapper is damp. What should she do?

options.A: Dry the outside wrapper carefully with a clean towel and use it
options.B: Check the chemical indicator strip and use the tray if the color changed
options.C: Consider the item contaminated and return it for re-sterilization
options.D: Open the package immediately before the moisture spreads further

explanation: Moisture on packaging acts like a sponge, pulling bacteria right through the barrier. It's best to safely reprocess it! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h7)

question: How does Maslow's hierarchy of needs apply to nursing school and patient care?

options.A: Basic survival and safety needs must be met before higher learning occurs
options.B: Classroom lectures should always focus on physical punishment
options.C: Students must memorize every medical diagnosis before touching a patient
options.D: Emotional support is completely secondary to technical skills

explanation: It's hard to focus on studying pathophysiology if you're exhausted, starving, or stressed about safety. Basic needs always come first for both students and patients! [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h5)

question: Why does the WHO stress having a steady supply of injection equipment?

options.A: Having extra supplies makes nurses finish their shifts much faster
options.B: Patients refuse treatment if clinics do not show them brand new boxes
options.C: Shortages often force workers to reuse single-use devices out of desperation
options.D: Government regulations require clinics to store at least ten years of stock

explanation: When clinics run out of disposables, it puts immense pressure on nurses. Reliable supplies keep everyone safe from risky workarounds. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h3)

question: What is the biggest benefit of asking a patient to keep a sleep diary for a couple of weeks?

options.A: It permanently cures nocturnal awakenings through auto-suggestion.
options.B: It measures blood oxygen saturation levels during REM sleep.
options.C: It provides a reliable, real-time record of actual sleep patterns and habits.
options.D: It replaces the need for any nursing or medical communication.

explanation: People aren't always great at remembering how they slept. A sleep diary captures daily habits and rest patterns in real time, giving nurses accurate info to work with. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T12#GNS123_U3_T12_h6)

question: Why is it important for a community nurse to understand disease agents?

options.A: To target specific causes when planning community disease prevention
options.B: To prescribe appropriate antibiotics without consulting a doctor
options.C: To accurately calculate hospital room bed turnover rates
options.D: To diagnose surgical complications before they become severe

explanation: When you know exactly what is causing an illness in your community, you can aim your prevention plans right at it and knock it out! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T78#GNS214_U1_T78_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of a Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM) sticker on a vaccine bottle?

options.A: To signal when the needle has been contaminated by bacteria
options.B: To show if the vial has been exposed to cumulative heat that could ruin its potency
options.C: To indicate the exact manufacturing date and batch number of the product
options.D: To measure the remaining volume of liquid inside the glass vial

explanation: The VVM is a nurse's best friend! It changes color when the vaccine has seen too much heat, letting you know instantly if it's still safe to use. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T70#GNS214_U1_T70_h8)

question: What should be included in a good community action plan?

options.A: An order for expensive medical equipment from foreign countries
options.B: A legal contract signed by every adult living in the district
options.C: A strict list of punishments for people who refuse to participate
options.D: Clear details on who will do what, when, and with what materials

explanation: An effective plan outlines specific roles, timelines, and resources so everyone knows their responsibilities. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h5)

question: What is the approximate percentage of sodium found in table salt by weight?

options.A: 10 percent
options.B: 40 percent
options.C: 90 percent
options.D: 75 percent

explanation: Table salt is sodium chloride, which breaks down to about 40 percent sodium and 60 percent chloride. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h4)

question: What are the three core components of the classic epidemiological triangle?

options.A: Vector, Patient, Hospital
options.B: Immunity, Sanitation, Treatment
options.C: Bacteria, Virus, Fungus
options.D: Agent, Host, Environment

explanation: Never forget the trio: the Agent (the germ), the Host (the person), and the Environment (where they meet). It's the bedrock of public health! [learn more](GNS313_U1_T2#GNS313_U1_T2_h4)

question: In what year was the VAPP Act passed into law in Nigeria to protect people against violence?
explanation: Spot on! The VAPP Act was enacted in May 2015 to give survivors a strong legal backing against domestic violence and abuse. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T14#GNS312_U4_T14_h1)

question: Which of the following is considered a late sign of low oxygen levels in the body?

options.A: Mild restlessness and anxiety
options.B: Leaning forward in a tripod position
options.C: Cyanosis or bluish skin discoloration
options.D: An increased breathing rate

explanation: Skin turning blue usually happens only after oxygen levels have dropped severely for some time. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T4#GNS212_U2_T4_h3)

question: Why is it so important to document a drug reaction in the notes and tell the patient about it?

options.A: To prevent the patient from receiving the same dangerous drug in the future
options.B: To satisfy legal insurance requirements for the nursing council
options.C: To prove to the doctor that the nurse made the correct diagnosis
options.D: To make sure the hospital pharmacy gets paid for the wasted medication

explanation: Clear records and patient education protect them from getting that same harmful drug again in future hospital visits. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T8#GNS125_U5_T8_h5)

question: Which hormone, released when you are under long-term stress, tends to lower your immune response?

options.A: Thyroxine
options.B: Cortisol
options.C: Melatonin
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Well done! High cortisol from chronic stress acts like a brake on your immune system, which is why stressed students easily catch colds during exams! [learn more](GNS123_U4_T2#GNS123_U4_T2_h6)

question: When a patient resists your care during a home visit, what does it most likely mean?

options.A: Proof that the patient has fully recovered from illness
options.B: Fear and a desire to retain personal control and independence
options.C: A deliberate plot to get the nurse fired from the agency
options.D: A lack of respect for human rights laws in medicine

explanation: Correct! Resistance is often just a defense mechanism. Patients are usually scared of losing their independence and are trying to hold onto control of their lives. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T4#GNS324_U2_T4_h6)

question: What important document must go with a patient when transferring her from a maternity home to a bigger hospital?

options.A: A clear and detailed referral note
options.B: A signed financial guarantee form
options.C: An inventory list of delivery room tools
options.D: A copy of the facility tax clearance certificate

explanation: Correct! The referral note tells the receiving team what has happened so far and what care she needs. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T15#GNS324_U5_T15_h7)

question: Why do community nurses love using practical cooking demonstrations with local foods?

options.A: They allow the nurse to sell cooking utensils to rural women
options.B: They show caregivers how to prepare affordable, nutrient-dense meals using familiar ingredients
options.C: They replace the need for hospital-based medical treatments entirely
options.D: They prove that imported foreign foods are superior to local produce

explanation: Well done! Cooking demos turn nutrition tips into real-life kitchen skills using food that families can easily find and afford locally. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h7)

question: Why must a nurse make sure a patient takes off any metal jewelry before an X-ray?

options.A: Metal items will permanently ruin the X-ray film
options.B: Metal objects block the rays and create artifacts
options.C: Metal interferes with the magnetic field used
options.D: Metal can absorb radiation and burn the skin

explanation: Metal blocks X-rays completely, leaving bright white spots on the image. These spots can hide fractures, so taking off jewelry or metal items is a quick safety step you won't want to miss. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T4#GNS222_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the correct temperature range for storing most routine vaccines in a clinic fridge?

options.C: +2°C to +8°C

explanation: You got it! Keeping vaccines between +2°C and +8°C keeps them fresh and effective without freezing them by accident. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T12#GNS313_U2_T12_h5)

question: Which duty can a home health aide safely perform for a client?

options.A: Adjusting the dosage of high blood pressure medication
options.B: Administering prescribed intravenous antibiotics
options.C: Evaluating the healing progress of a surgical wound
options.D: Assisting with personal hygiene and bathing

explanation: Home health aides are trained to help with activities of daily living, such as bathing, grooming, and basic personal care. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h3)

question: Why are daily weight checks such an important nursing tool when managing fluid and electrolyte imbalances?

options.A: Body weight dictates the exact dosage of every routine antibiotic
options.B: Changes in weight provide a reliable daily measure of fluid gain or loss
options.C: Sudden weight loss always proves that kidney function has fully recovered
options.D: Weight records replace the need to monitor urinary output in bedridden patients

explanation: Spot on! A sudden change in weight over 24 hours isn't fat or muscle—it's almost always a shift in body water. Daily weights help us catch fluid overload early! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T9#GNS123_U2_T9_h6)

question: What is a helpful technique when a Parkinson's patient suddenly 'freezes' and cannot move their feet while walking?

options.A: Firmly push the patient forward from behind to restart momentum
options.B: Instruct the patient to lean backward to shift their center of gravity
options.C: Tell the patient to close their eyes and try to run quickly
options.D: Ask the patient to step over a visual cue on the floor or count out loud

explanation: Freezing can be scary! Using a visual trick—like stepping over a line on the floor—or counting a steady rhythm gives the brain a new cue to help break the freeze. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T4#GNS222_U4_T4_h7)

question: A 34-week pregnant mum comes in with painless, bright red vaginal bleeding. What condition should you suspect first?

options.A: Placenta previa
options.B: Placenta accreta
options.C: Chorioamnionitis
options.D: Placental abruption

explanation: Spot on! Classic textbook sign: painless, bright red bleeding late in pregnancy is a major red flag for placenta previa, where the placenta sits low over the cervix. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T008#GNS226_U2_T008_h7)

question: How does severe dehydration affect the skin?

options.A: It permanently changes the natural pigmentation of the skin
options.B: It speeds up the healing rate of minor skin abrasions
options.C: It causes an overproduction of natural skin oils
options.D: It reduces blood flow and impairs cellular metabolism

explanation: Well done! When your body lacks water, blood flow to the skin slows down, starving the cells and making the skin weak and fragile. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h3)

question: Why must nurse researchers pay close attention to ethics during explanatory studies?

options.A: Because ethics boards only approve studies written in foreign languages
options.B: Because testing new interventions or manipulating variables can potentially affect patient safety
options.C: Because hospital patients prefer answering long questionnaires over resting
options.D: Because research ethics only apply to doctors and never to nurses

explanation: You nailed it! Whenever we test new methods or change care routines, keeping our patients safe is always the top priority. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T13#GNS224_U1_T13_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal complication of being unconscious and immobile for a long time?

options.A: Muscle contractures and joint stiffness
options.B: Deep vein thrombosis in the lower legs
options.C: Pressure ulcers on bony prominences

options.A: Body Mass Index calculator
options.B: Glasgow Coma Scale
options.C: Apgar scoring system
options.D: Geriatric Depression Scale

question: Which drug is a main part of the preferred first-line HIV treatment guidelines in Nigeria?

options.C: Zidovudine
options.D: Nevirapine

question: Why is finding protein persistently in a patient's urine an important warning sign?

options.A: It confirms that the liver is failing to process dietary nutrients properly.
options.B: It shows that the bladder is contracting too frequently during the day.
options.C: It indicates that the filtering barriers of the glomeruli have been damaged.
options.D: It proves that the patient is eating too much protein in their daily diet.

explanation: Healthy glomeruli act like a strict bouncer, keeping big protein molecules safely inside the blood. If protein leaks into the urine, it tells us those filters are injured. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T7#GNS213_U4_T7_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical motor symptom of degenerative neurological disorders?

options.A: Muscle stiffness
options.B: Balance problems
options.C: Tremors at rest
options.D: Sudden acute pain

question: What is often the very first sign that a patient is bleeding after having their tonsils out?

question: An elderly client with limited mobility spends most of the day lying in bed. What is the most important preventive action the caregiver should take?

options.C: Reposition the client frequently to protect skin integrity
options.D: Restrict all fluid intake to prevent bathroom accidents

question: A patient with known esophageal varices is admitted to the ward. Which diet should the nurse encourage?

options.C: Increasing dietary fiber with raw, crunchy vegetables
options.D: Eating soft, non-abrasive foods to prevent vessel rupture

question: During a shift handover, which drug history detail is most critical to share?

question: What is the main goal of the DASH diet for someone with high blood pressure?

question: After a safe delivery, which eye ointment do you apply right away to protect a newborn from eye infections?

question: Why is it important for nurses to ask patients about traditional or local remedies they might be using?

question: Why is it important to dim the lights in the examination room before starting?

options.D: Bright light causes the ophthalmoscope bulb to burn out quickly
